run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The traced failure path is frontend -> search -> rate. Every /hotels request observed fails with HTTP 500 because search's Nearby call to rate fails: search's client spans to /rate.Rate/GetRates end at its 750 ms deadline, and search logs 'downstream request failed dependency=rate' with grpc_code DeadlineExceeded and ResourceExhausted. Inside rate, successful /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans take ~12.74-12.80 s while its only observed backend child (memcached_get_multi_rate) runs for 0.3-0.7 ms and starts about 12.7 s after the server span began, so the time is spent inside rate ahead of its backend call; some rate server spans end in error almost instantly (20-36 us), matching the ResourceExhausted rejections logged by search. The rate Deployment's pod template carries RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256, settings present only in rate among the namespace's 19 deployments; an admission wait of ~256/20 = 12.8 s matches the observed ~12.7 s. Pods are all Running/ready with 0 restarts, endpoints are populated, geo/profile/reservation show no error evidence, and the sampled mongodb-rate logs show a normal startup with no slow queries. The fault therefore originates in the rate service's throttling/queue configuration, with search's aggressive 3-attempt 750 ms retry policy amplifying load and latency-to-failure. The conclusion is partial: no pre-18:02 baseline exists (the whole namespace was created at 18:02:11-18:02:23) and the rate-side limiter/queue internals were not directly observable.

claims.text: All 19 hotel-reservation deployments report 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready replica; all 19 pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState.terminated, and they were created between 18:02:11Z and 18:02:23Z, so no crash loop, OOMKill or eviction is present in the workload.

The rate Deployment's container 'hotel-reserv-rate' sets env RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256; these two variables appear on no other deployment in hotel-reservation (all others set only JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO, MEMCACHED_* or nothing). The rate Deployment is deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1 / generation 1 and its kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration contains both variables, i.e. the throttling settings are part of the pod template that produced pod rate-c4d7bcb48-4wrxs.

The search Deployment's container 'hotel-reserv-search' sets the rate client policy RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0 and RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2.

Trace 2b92984f259d7cc8 and its siblings show frontend span 'HTTP GET /hotels' with status error=true, http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR lasting 1.63-2.41 s, with child frontend span '/search.Search/Nearby' in ERROR, child search span '/search.Search/Nearby' in ERROR, and search-side client spans '/rate.Rate/GetRates' in ERROR; in that sample 3 of 3 /hotels spans and 3 of 3 search server spans errored.

search's client spans to /rate.Rate/GetRates fail at its configured deadline: in the 3-trace frontend error sample, 9 of 9 search->rate client spans are ERROR with durations 750051-750942 us, and one attempt of 568 us (trace 6b1a1f2888832028) is paired with a rate server span of 20 us that also carries error=true/otel.status_code=ERROR.

rate's own server spans /rate.Rate/GetRates (service rate) run 12736616-12798937 us (~12.74-12.80 s), while its client span memcached_get_multi_rate for the same requests runs only 330-509 us and starts ~12.7 s after the server span start (e.g. server 4d91c06a768cb52a at 1795284254324542 lasting 12781566 us, memcached child 585eb6c556a77d59 at 1795284267105720 lasting 344 us), so the delay elapses inside rate before its backend call.

Pod search-7769dfc66b-2q9xr logs 'downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded' and '...dependency=rate grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' repeatedly (e.g. 18:04:05.70Z through 18:04:12.93Z, newest 60 of 803 matching lines shown).
The Loki count of those 'downstream request failed' lines in search rises from 700 to 803 between 18:04:00Z and 18:04:13Z, i.e. roughly 7-8 failed rate attempts per second at the end of the window.

In the Prometheus increase query grouped by service_name, span_name and status_code, the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR series returned for the whole namespace was search's span_name '/rate.Rate/GetRates' (2307.9) against its STATUS_CODE_UNSET count (98.3); no other service/operation produced an ERROR series in that query, and rate itself returned only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (3010.9). Note this metric records some spans that carry otel.status_code=ERROR in Jaeger as UNSET, so trace status tags are the stronger error evidence here.

The geo dependency is fast and error-free in the same traces: geo server spans '/geo.Geo/Nearby' last 28-44 us with status not_recorded and search's client '/geo.Geo/Nearby' spans last 827-1008 us with no error tag, in contrast to the 750 ms failing rate calls.

The rate Service has a live endpoint (10.244.7.195 on port 8084, plus 9091), and every other hotel-reservation Service also has at least one address, so name resolution/endpoint wiring for rate is populated.

All 19 hotel-reservation workloads were scaled from 0 to 1 by their own Deployments at 18:02:11-18:02:13Z (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet -> ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate -> Pod Scheduled/Created/Started, e.g. 'Scaled up replica set rate-c4d7bcb48 from 0 to 1'), including the rate pod at 18:02:12-18:02:19Z; this is environment provisioning at the start of the window, not a later targeted rollout.

The sampled mongodb-rate log (newest 60 of 212 lines) shows a normal startup: 'Waiting for connections' on 27017, successful SCRAM-SHA-1 authentication, creation of rate-db.inventory with a hotelId_1 index, a routine checkpoint at 18:03:19Z, and no error or slow-query entries in the lines read.

The rate container log contains only startup lines ending 18:02:19Z ('Starting server...', consul registration 'srv-rate' at 10.244.7.195:8084) and no request-time error lines, so rate's failures are visible only through its spans and through search's logs.

The frontend container log lines read contain only startup output ending 18:02:13Z (including consul connection-refused retries while consul was still starting); no application-level error line is present, so the /hotels 500s are evidenced by the frontend spans rather than by its logs.

The rate Deployment's throttling configuration is the fault mechanism: backend work is admitted at RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 ops/s behind a RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 queue, so requests observe an admission wait of about 256/20 = 12.8 s (matching the measured ~12.74-12.80 s rate server spans that complete a sub-millisecond backend call only at the end) and newly arriving calls are rejected immediately with gRPC ResourceExhausted (the 20-36 us ERROR rate spans and the 'grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' search log lines).

Search's client policy (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 with RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 and 50 ms initial backoff) converts the rate slowness into fast, repeated failures and multiplies the offered load on the saturated rate queue by up to 3 attempts per Nearby call; it amplifies the incident but cannot explain the ~12.7 s server-side latency measured inside rate itself.

mongodb-rate being the slow dependency is not supported: rate's ~12.7 s elapses before its only observed backend child call, and that child (memcached_get_multi_rate) completes in 330-509 us; the sampled mongodb-rate log shows normal startup/authentication and no slow-query or error entries. This does not fully exclude mongo: rate's mongo_rate child spans for those requests would start after the ~12.7 s mark, i.e. after the authorized window end, so their latency is unknown.

Kubernetes-level failure (crash, OOMKill, eviction, not-ready pod, missing endpoints) is not supported for this incident: all pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts and empty last termination reasons, the hotel-reservation events are Normal provisioning events only (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, PVC provisioning), and the rate Service has a populated endpoint.

The non-rate dependency paths show no failure signal of their own: geo server spans are 28-44 us with no error status, and the grouped metric query returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for profile.Profile/GetProfiles, reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability or geo.Geo/Nearby, i.e. nothing observed implicates geo, profile or reservation in this fault (note STATUS_CODE_UNSET does not by itself mean success).

Review the rate Deployment's RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 against the intended capacity for this workload (raise or remove the throttle), then re-check search's 'downstream request failed dependency=rate' rate and the frontend /hotels 500 rate.

Review search's rate client retry policy (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3) so retries do not multiply load on a throttled dependency, and add rate-side queue-depth/rejection counters (the current rate container log shows nothing at request time) to make the limiter visible.

gaps: No baseline before 18:02: the entire namespace was created/scaled at 18:02:11-18:02:23Z and all available metric series begin then, so latency and error levels cannot be compared with a healthy period and I cannot determine whether the rate throttling settings were newly introduced or shipped from the start (rate Deployment is generation 1/revision 1).

The rate limiter/queue internals were not directly observable: there is no queue-depth, rejection or throttle metric among the available series (only traces_span_metrics_calls_total exists for this app), so the ~12.7 s = 256/20 queue-drain inference is a hypothesis, not a measured queue state.

rate's mongo_rate child spans for the affected requests start after the ~12.7 s admission wait, i.e. after the authorized window end (18:04:13Z), so the latency of rate's MongoDB calls during the incident is unknown and mongodb-rate cannot be fully cleared.
The NetworkPolicy check for hotel-reservation returned no data (0 items), so policy-level causes can be neither confirmed nor ruled out.
Jaeger lists traces for only 6 services (frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search); recommendation and user have no trace data in this Run, so their health is unobserved.
The mongodb-rate log read was truncated to the newest 60 of 212 lines and the rate/frontend log reads end at startup, so their older or later lines are unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so when and by whom the rate env settings were applied cannot be verified.
next_steps: Compare the rate Deployment manifest (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY) with the intended baseline manifest or change history for this scenario to confirm the injected values.
After adjusting the rate throttle, verify recovery by watching search spans '/rate.Rate/GetRates' error status, rate server span durations, and frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' http.status_code=500 spans.
Add rate-side observability (queue depth, rejections, backend-call latency) and mongo_rate span coverage so the admission wait and backend time can be separated.
Re-check mongodb-rate latency once traces from rate's post-wait backend calls are inside a query window.
